gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
She can't afford ___ her car repaired this month.
gaps.explanation: afford + to-infinitive: can't afford to get.

gaps.sentence: Do you know how ___ this machine?
gaps.explanation: know how/what/where + to-infinitive: know how to operate.

gaps.sentence: I tried ___ the shelf up, but it was too heavy.
gaps.explanation: try + to-infinitive = attempt, make an effort.

gaps.sentence: The hotel offered ___ our room free of charge.
gaps.explanation: offer takes the to-infinitive: offered to upgrade.

gaps.sentence: I've always wanted ___ how to sail.
The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: Do you fancy ___ to the cinema tonight?
gaps.explanation: fancy + -ing (informal British): Do you fancy going…?
